details: A deepening global selloff in semiconductor stocks, intensified on Friday, has dragged down broader risk assets, including Bitcoin. This rout stems from investor concerns about whether massive gains fueled by artificial intelligence can justify elevated valuations. Tech-heavy indexes like the Nasdaq 100 experienced significant declines, with major chipmakers seeing substantial losses. Bitcoin, sensitive to overall market risk appetite, slipped alongside traditional equities.
title: Global Tech Selloff Deepens, Weighing on Risk Assets

details: US consumer price index (CPI) data, showing a deceleration to 3.5% from 4.2%, has significantly improved macro liquidity expectations and boosted risk appetite for cryptocurrencies. Polymarket traders now place a 94% probability on the Federal Reserve holding interest rates steady at its upcoming July 28-29 meeting. This easing of inflation concerns and reduced expectations for further tightening have led to renewed institutional demand, with spot Bitcoin ETFs recording $132.3 million in net inflows on July 17.
title: Softer US Inflation Boosts Bitcoin, Fed Rate Hold Odds Climb

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has issued a warning that the unchecked growth of dollar-denominated stablecoins could significantly erode the deposit base of European banks, posing a challenge to monetary policy. ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone highlighted that if consumers and businesses increasingly hold funds in stablecoins like Tether's USDT or Circle's USDC, these funds exit the European banking system. This concern underpins the ECB's push for a digital euro as a countermeasure to maintain financial stability and the central bank's role in payments.
title: ECB Warns Stablecoin Growth Threatens Bank Deposits
